title: How long does a red blood cell live?
hook: Your blood is renewing as you read: red blood cells live about four months on average.
summary: Red blood cells live about 120 days on average, while bone marrow produces new blood cells.
cardText: A red blood cell lives about 120 days on average. Bone marrow makes new cells, keeping blood renewed and oxygen moving through the body.

cardBlocks.text: A red blood cell lives about 120 days on average: roughly four months rather than seven years. As blood cells die, replacements are made in bone marrow, the spongy tissue inside bones. Blood renewal is a continuing process, rather than a single event that replaces everything at once.

Red cells carry oxygen with the help of a protein called hemoglobin. Each has a disc shape with a shallow dip on both sides. Mature red cells have no nucleus and can change shape easily, helping them pass through blood vessels. But circulation also damages their membrane and depletes their energy supplies, limiting their lifespan.
Red cells live about four months on average; bone marrow keeps producing new blood cells.

deepDiveBlocks.text: Blood has more than one timetable
In bone marrow, stem cells give rise to different blood components. These cells can produce descendants that specialize, including red and white blood cells.

White blood cells help defend against infection. Platelets are cell fragments involved in clotting, the process that forms a clot at a wound. These components do not all last equally long: some white cells live less than a day, while others live much longer.

Blood is not all cells. More than half its volume is plasma, the liquid part containing water, salts and proteins. Replacing red cells and maintaining that liquid are different aspects of how blood works.
